title: A-V-L

cards: Three friends hear that a man named Job has lost everything: his animals, his servants, his children, and now his health. They set out from home and meet up to go to him together.
From a distance they hardly recognize him. They weep, they tear their robes, they throw dust in the air. Then they do the thing the book remembers.
They sit down with him on the ground, for seven days and seven nights, and nobody says a word. Later, they'll talk, and the talking won't go well. But the first week, they got exactly right.

teach.h: JACOB: I WILL GO DOWN MOURNING.
teach.b: A-V-L. Alef, vet, lamed. Avel: a mourner.
Avelut: the time of mourning. First, a father in Genesis. Jacob's sons bring him their brother Joseph's coat, torn and bloodied, and he believes Joseph is dead.
His children come to comfort him, and he won't be comforted. "For I will go down into the grave unto my son mourning." Mourning there is avel: not a passing sadness, a state you live in.

Second, Job's friends. The text says why they kept silent: "for they saw that his grief was very great." The rabbis turned that silence into a custom: visitors to a house of mourning wait for the mourner to speak first.
You don't arrive with a speech. You arrive. Third, the shape of the time.
The first week after a burial is shiva, from the word for seven.

teach.h: SHIVA: THE COMMUNITY COMES TO YOU.
teach.b: The mourners stay home, often sitting low, and the community comes to them, bringing food and filling the room so the prayers can be said there. Then the mourning loosens in stages, over the following weeks and the year.
Grief isn't told to be over by a date. It's given rooms to move through. Fourth, the comforters' words.
When visitors leave a house of mourning, the traditional line asks that God comfort the mourner among the mourners of Zion and Jerusalem.
Even the comfort puts the mourner inside a larger group. An avel is someone the community is holding up.

how: Jewish mourners sit shiva, staying home after the burial while the community visits, brings food and makes up a prayer quorum; by custom visitors wait for the mourner to speak first, and on leaving they offer the traditional words of comfort.

games.q: you and two friends reach Job, who has lost everything. you can hardly recognize him. what do you do?
o: sit down with him on the ground and say nothing.
games.why: they sat with him seven days and seven nights, and none spoke a word, for they saw his grief was very great.

practice: Bring to mind someone who is grieving, recently or years ago, and simply sit with them in your mind, the way Job's friends sat on the ground; you don't have to fix it or find words.
If you're the one mourning, let yourself be sat with, and if you pray, you can hold them in your prayer.
If grief ever feels like too much to carry, please reach out: in the US, call or text 988, any hour; elsewhere, local emergency help.
